w:r.w:t: PRD – Executive Summary through Future Scope

MedPredict AI is a cloud-native, explainable AI platform that ingests structured patient health parameters and returns multi-class disease risk probabilities for Diabetes, Heart Disease, Hypertension, and a Healthy baseline. Every prediction is accompanied by SHAP-driven explanations, actionable clinical recommendations, and a downloadable PDF report — enabling clinicians and patients to understand not just what the model predicts, but why.

Chronic diseases (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, hypertension) account for over 74% of global deaths annually. Primary care physicians face time constraints that reduce preventive screening quality. Patients lack tools to self-monitor multi-disease risk from home. Existing EHR-embedded models are black boxes that erode clinician trust.

There is no accessible, explainable, multi-disease risk tool that a GP can deploy in under 5 minutes, that a patient can operate without medical literacy, and that produces evidence-grade audit trails for clinical governance.

This is a multi-class classification problem. We map each patient record to one of four labels: Diabetes (0), Heart Disease (1), Hypertension (2), Healthy (3). The model must handle overlapping clinical features across diseases (e.g., BMI and blood pressure appear in all three), so a unified feature space across merged datasets is essential.
Step 1 – Domain knowledge filter: retain clinically validated markers
Step 2 – Univariate chi² / ANOVA-F against target label
Step 4 – Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) with Random Forest estimator
Step 5 – Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) < 10 to remove multicollinear features
Justification: combining statistical + model-based + medical validation reduces both overfitting and clinician distrust of irrelevant inputs

Decision Tree · Random Forest · XGBoost · Ensemble

Each algorithm has complementary inductive biases. Decision Trees provide interpretable splitting logic. Random Forest reduces variance through bagging. XGBoost reduces both bias and variance through gradient boosting. Ensemble voting combines their posterior probabilities, empirically outperforming any single base model on tabular medical data.

SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) provides game-theory-grounded attribution of each feature to the prediction output. Unlike LIME (which is unstable) or attention weights (which are model-specific), SHAP satisfies consistency, dummy, and efficiency axioms. TreeExplainer is O(TLD²) for tree models, making it tractable for real-time clinical use.
